title: Result Table: Sort Students by Marks
statement: Read n student records. Each record has a name and marks. Print a table sorted by marks, highest first. If two students have the same marks, put the name that comes first in ASCII order (the order strcmp uses) first. Capital letters come before small letters. Print a header line and a line of 16 dashes. Print each name left-aligned in 10 characters, then one space, then marks right-aligned in 5 characters.
inputFormat: First line: n. Then n lines, each with a name (one word, letters only) and an integer mark, separated by one space.
outputFormat: Header "Name" (width 10), a space, "Marks" (width 5, right-aligned). Then 16 dashes. Then n rows in sorted order, formatted like the header.
explanations: Ravi has 92, Meena 85, Asha 78. So the order is by marks, highest first.
Zoya has 90 and is first. Amit, Bala and Kiran all have 70, so they are sorted by name.
reference:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
recs = []
for i in range(n):
    name = data[1 + 2 * i]
    marks = int(data[2 + 2 * i])
    recs.append((name, marks))
recs.sort(key=lambda r: (-r[1], r[0]))
print(f"{'Name':<10} {'Marks':>5}")
print("-" * 16)
for name, marks in recs:
    print(f"{name:<10} {marks:>5}")
